2608.30828.title: Opinionated, Hesitant and Stressed: Three Studies of How Politicians Speak in Four Slavic Parliaments
2608.30828.paper_summary: We present three large-scale studies of spoken parliamentary speech across four Slavic languages (Croatian, Czech, Polish, Serbian), drawing on over 6,000 hours from the ParlaSpeech 3.0 corpus. The first study examines how utterance-level sentiment shapes acoustic realisation: negative speech is consistently produced with higher pitch, greater intensity, and faster rate across all four parliaments, with a secondary arousal-driven upturn at the most positive extreme. The second study models filled pause frequency using negative binomial GEE, finding that speech rate, age, and sentiment are robust cross-lingual predictors, while gender effects reverse between South Slavic (men produce fewer filled pauses) and West Slavic parliaments (no gender difference) - a pattern invisible to single-language designs. The third study investigates primary stress variation in Croatian, showing that speaker-level preferences for early versus late stress cohere across verbs, adjectives, and nouns but decouple for adverbs and proper nouns. We conclude with a research agenda spanning corpus phonetics, disfluency modelling, and political rhetoric.
2608.30828.paper_summary_zh: 我們呈現了三項針對四種斯拉夫語言（克羅埃西亞語、捷克語、波蘭語、塞爾維亞語）的口語議會演講的大型研究，這些研究基於超過6,000小時的ParlaSpeech 3.0語料庫。第一項研究檢視了語句層面的情感如何影響聲學實現：在所有四個議會中，負面言論的產出均一致地表現出更高的音調、更大的強度和更快的語速，在最積極的極端還出現了由喚起驅動的次要上升。第二項研究使用負二項廣義估計方程模型填充停頓的頻率，發現語速、年齡和情感是穩健的跨語言預測因子，而性別效應在南斯拉夫語（男性產生較少的填充停頓）和西斯拉夫語議會（性別差異不存在）之間相反——這一模式在單語言設計中是不可見的。第三項研究探討了克羅埃西亞語中的主要重音變化，顯示說話者對早期與晚期重音的偏好在動詞、形容詞和名詞中是一致的，但在副詞和專有名詞中則分離。我們以涵蓋語料音韻學、流暢性建模和政治修辭的研究議程作結。
2608.30828.author: Ivan Porupski et.al.
